title: avatar_url across five layers: the mega-task temptation
description: Type H (oversized leaf). The feature is small in code volume but touches five files across five layers (model, validators, service, handlers, serializers). The natural anti-plan is one task 'implement avatar_url' owning all five files — a phase-shaped leaf that no single fresh executor can close without reading everything. Good plans split along the layer closures (each task 1-2 anchors, 3-6 tasks total), freeze the two cross-layer contracts (owner-only rule; public-JSON omission rule), and gate the e2e path (handler -> service -> model -> serializer) including the non-owner rejection and the key-omission behavior.

must_freeze.note: the owner-only rule (user_id == profile_id, existing PermissionError path) is a cross-layer contract that avatar_url must ride on, not duplicate
public JSON omission rule: key absent (not null/empty) when avatar_url is unset — a consumer contract

parallelizable_groups.note: model change and validator change are disjoint closures; both feed the service join point

expected.notes: Type H probe: leaf boundedness. A single task owning >2 anchors (the mega 'avatar feature' task) is the flagship anti-plan — caught by max_anchors_per_task, acceptable_task_count_range, and phase_shaped_leaves. Invented scope (file storage, upload endpoint, DB migration) is the secondary bait — the task is URL-only, no storage.
